> 頤。貞吉。觀頤，自求口實。

Hexagram 27 is about the jaw, and the book insists on separating the shape of the character from the meaning the classic gives it.

## 頤 is a jaw, and 養 is an extension

The original sense is the cheek, the jowl.

朵頤 — the jaw working, cheeks bulging — uses exactly that original sense.

And the distinction: the character describes the cheek; the classic's sense, 養 — to nourish — comes from the fact that the mouth is where food enters and the body is fed. "Nourish" is not in the shape. It arrives one step later.

So the hexagram is about feeding, and the word it starts from is the part of the face that chews.

## 觀頤，自求口實

Watch what feeds what, and seek your own mouth's substance.

The judgement sets the hexagram's two questions in one line: observe the feeding arrangement, and take responsibility for your own intake.

Which already rules out both failure modes the lines will show: watching others' mouths, and expecting someone else to fill yours.

## 靈龜: the turtle that does not eat

初九 舍爾靈龜，觀我朵頤，凶.

The turtle is still and does not eat; it sustains itself by breath. 靈 here is not "numinous" in a magical sense — it is the layer of not depending on anything outside.

So the line: you have set aside the creature that feeds itself, and you are watching my jaw work.

凶. Not "it is bad to be hungry." It is: throwing away self-sufficiency to envy someone else's eating.

## 顛頤, used twice, judged two ways

顛 is to invert. The normal order is that the upper feeds the lower; 顛 reverses it.

六二 顛頤，拂經；于丘頤，征凶.
六四 顛頤，吉；虎視眈眈，其欲逐逐，無咎.

Same word, opposite verdicts — and this is the chapter's most important case of 同詞異斷.

The difference is the direction of power. Line 2 is a yielding line in a yielding place, and it inverts the order to feed itself upward — that is 拂經, against the constant. Line 4 is a yielding line in a firm place, directly under the ruler, and it inverts the order to supply what is above it: it is feeding upward on behalf of the whole, and the text approves.

So 顛 is not the fault. The fault is inverting the order for oneself.

## 虎視眈眈，其欲逐逐

眈眈: the gaze fixed and intent.

逐逐 has two readings: pursuing in sequence, one after another; or 敦實, honest and single-minded (釋文: 敦實貌).

This book takes the first: the desire to nourish is present, and it pursues with measure, not in a flood.

Which is the difference between appetite and greed, and the line applies it to the one place where appetite is correct: supplying someone else.

## 由頤

Top line: 由頤，厲吉，利涉大川.

由: from, by way of. All under heaven is fed by way of this line — the top of the nourishing, the master of the provision.

厲吉, dangerous and good. The highest position in a feeding system is the most exposed one: everyone's intake depends on it, and there is no one above to correct it.

## 慎言語，節飲食

The 象: be careful with words, regulate food and drink.

言語 goes out as breath; 飲食 comes in as form. Both are gateways of 精氣.

Which is why the two are put together: they are the same kind of boundary, one outbound and one inbound, and the discipline of the hexagram is the discipline of what crosses them.

## The test

Take a dependency in your life — someone you feed, someone who feeds you. Ask the inverted question: is the arrangement upside down, and is it upside down for the sake of the whole or for the sake of the one? 六二 and 六四 are the same posture with two verdicts, and the distinction is not visible from outside.
